preamble: Method: Solve the clues and fit the solutions into the diagram jigsaw-wise, wherever they will go.

clue.text: Bird won't pay dues, they say, to fly round head

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the words before it are judged by sound

parts.note: someone who will not settle up yet will owe
the warble fly lays eggs whose larvae raise swellings, called warbles, under the skin of cattle; one that warbles is a warbler

explanation.surface: A bird that won't pay its dues is said to fly round someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria leans on the warble fly for the second half; the first half is a straight sound-alike of 'will owe'.
explanation.definitionFit: The willow warbler is a small migrant songbird common in European woodland and gardens.

clue.text: See 1 across
His merry creature formerly was matched

definitions.text: His merry creature formerly was matched

parts.words: His merry creature formerly was matched
parts.note: surface reading: some happy animal that once had a partner of the same kind; setter's reading: a woman who was once married is a widow, and his merry one is the title of his famous operetta

explanation.surface: A cheerful animal belonging to some man used to have a mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formerly was matched' describes a widow, once wed; the Merry Widow is the operetta that made its composer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár, the Hungarian-Austrian composer, wrote The Merry Widow, so the widow is his creation.

clue.text: Call to write tune sub divo (under God)

parts.note: O is the vocative call, as in 'O Lord'
to pen is to write
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: An appeal to compose a melody, in Latin, beneath the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: Sub divo is Latin for 'under the sky', literally 'under the god'; the bracket glosses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done beneath the open sky, outdoors rather than indoors, is literally what the Latin phrase means.

clue.text: With status odd, sufficient to proceed

parts.note: the word that keeps company with status in the Latin phrase status quo
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone of strange rank is nonetheless enough to let things go ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A quorum is the minimum number of members present that lets a meeting legally conduct business.

clue.text: Rough: striking into (starter missing) meal

indicators.note: one thing going into another sits inside it
a meal served without its first course has lost its opening, so the word drops its initial letter

parts.note: lunch is a meal
workers on strike are out

explanation.surface: A crude scene: someone bursting into a dinner that has no first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncouth manners are coarse and unpolished, which is one sense of rough behaviour.

clue.text: It's true about the country's second read

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: something true is real
Peru is the country, with its possessive s

explanation.surface: A claim about a nation is genuine, says someone reading it over again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The country' could be any nation; the letters available make it Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to read carefully, so going through it again is a second perusal.

clue.text: Empress, Australian devotee of dance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the twelfth-century claimant to the English throne, wife of the Holy Roman Emperor
second meaning: the swag in the bush ballad, always waltzing

explanation.walkthrough: In Australian slang a swagman's bedroll is his matilda, and 'Waltzing Matilda' is the country's best-loved song.
explanation.definitionFit: Empress Matilda fought Stephen for England; the song character is forever waltzing, hence a devotee of dancing.

clue.text: I'm on one side, I like to be in bed

indicators.note: being in a place means lying inside it, so these letters go within the next word

parts.note: taken as written
as means like
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lying on one side of the mattress says they like staying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person: the answer describes itself as partial.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prejudiced means favouring one party, standing on one side of an argument.

clue.text: Church job: Scots boy is one with fuzz in head

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the word after it

parts.note: Archie is a typically Scottish boy's name
pate is an old word for head
taken as written
the fuzz is slang for the police, and one of them is a cop

explanation.surface: A Scottish lad lands a church post despite having fluff on his head.
explanation.definitionFit: The archiepiscopate is the office or tenure of an archbishop, a senior post in the church.

clue.text: In service, girl? Will love a girl deliver?

indicators.note: to deliver is to set free, and freed letters fall into a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl in domestic service is asked whether, out of love, she will deliver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In service' sounds like a housemaid's job but means a church service; the girl's name is a bonus hint.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gloria is a hymn of praise sung as part of the Mass and other liturgies.

clue.text: Half soldier's trust: so blame at feet is laid

definitions.text: so blame at feet is laid

indicators.note: half means only one of two equal parts survives, so the rest is cut away

parts.note: a squaddie is British slang for a private soldier
to rely on is to trust

explanation.surface: An army half-trusted: the soldier gets the blame laid at his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Squaddie is British slang for a private; only its first four letters are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Blame is said to be laid squarely at someone's feet, the adverb meaning directly and fully.

clue.text: Container port like scene of bombers' drops

parts.note: a crate is a container
port is a red wine, and a ship's port light is red

explanation.surface: A shipping dock, its boxes stacked, resembles a place where bombs have fallen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground hit by bombs is pitted with holes blasted by explosions, which is what cratered describes.

clue.text: Bent's about right and cruel as de Sade

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps the next

parts.note: something bent and twisting is tortuous
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A crooked man is right about it, and as cruel as the notorious Marquis.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marquis de Sade relished inflicting pain, and something torturous involves causing great agony.

clue.text: Soldier on horseback comes to fish a river

parts.note: huss is the British trade name for dogfish sold in fish shops
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A cavalryman rides up to go fishing on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a light cavalryman, originally from the Hungarian mounted regiments.

clue.text: If God wills, or a king, I could do ops

parts.note: DV stands for Deo volente, Latin for 'God willing'
taken as written
taken as written
K is king in chess and card notation

explanation.surface: A surgeon, God or a monarch willing, says they could perform operations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ops' looks surgical but is the plural of op, short for opus, a numbered musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonín Dvořák, the Czech composer, numbered his compositions by opus, so he could write ops.

clue.text: Smooth: check your leader — first, a cut of veal

indicators.note: with a cut away, the word loses that one letter

parts.note: taken as written
to vet is to check

indicators.note: the leader is the first in line, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of your

explanation.surface: A chef tells you to inspect the boss's veal and slice off a smooth cut first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' moves the trimmed veal to the front of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Velvety means soft and smooth to the touch, like the fabric velvet.

clue.text: Make friends with painter, having strings attached

parts.note: kith are friends, as in kith and kin
ARA is Associate of the Royal Academy, a painter's title

explanation.surface: Befriending an artist always comes with conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strings attached' sounds like hidden conditions; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The kithara was an ancient Greek lyre, an instrument fitted with strings.

clue.text: See 18 down
Maslanka's work (see Sport) — cry "Pig!" — weird, odd

indicators.note: weird means strange or out of the ordinary, so the words are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
something odd is puzzling

explanation.surface: Someone shouts an insult at a strange, odd person, as reported on the sports pages.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Maslanka set cricket-based brainteasers called Pyrgic Puzzles in the Guardian's Sport section.
explanation.definitionFit: Maslanka's regular puzzle feature was titled Pyrgic Puzzles, pyrgic being his coinage for cricket-related.

clue.text: I did protest: last fliers take a pound

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
a wing is an air force unit of fliers
L, from libra, is the symbol for a pound
a means one, written as the Roman I

explanation.surface: A protester boasts that the final pilots were charged a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound and the 'a' join in reverse order: the one comes after the pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Huldrych Zwingli led the Reformation in Zurich, a founding Protestant who could say he protested.

clue.text: Could there be tin here? Or the rein, perchance?

definitions.text: Could there be tin here? Or the rein, perchance?

indicators.note: asking what something could be invites rearranging it into another form
perchance suggests a chance arrangement, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled question: is there tin here, or perhaps a rein?
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'tin here' and 'the rein' rearrange to the answer, which is also the reply to the question.
explanation.definitionFit: Asked whether it is one thing or another, the reply 'not one, nor the other' answers both possibilities.

clue.text: A new leaf turn: as brass I shall be bold

definitions.text: as brass I shall be bold

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone promises to turn over a new leaf and act boldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A new leaf' tempts the solver to use the A; only 'leaf turn' is rearranged. Brass here is cheek, nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: One who flaunts shows off brazenly, with the nerve and showiness that brass and boldness suggest.

clue.text: I'm loth to quarrel: anger's less than E

parts.note: ire is anger
nic, nicotine, is a lesser drug than E, ecstasy

explanation.surface: A peacemaker says their temper is less than extreme.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the slang for the drug ecstasy; nicotine is the milder fix.
explanation.definitionFit: Irenic means peaceable, tending toward conciliation, from the Greek word for peace.

clue.text: Take penalty with ordinance that's old

definitions.note: the verb is exacting a penalty, so the definition reads as taking one

parts.note: ex means former
an act is a law or ordinance

explanation.surface: Someone enforces a punishment under a long-repealed decree.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old' piece comes first in the answer although it is last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact a penalty is to demand and inflict it, so exacting is taking a penalty.

clue.text: To see the unseen, crazed Haig or proxy read

indicators.note: crazed means driven mad, so the words that follow are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A deranged general Haig has a stand-in read his orders aloud to reveal hidden things.
explanation.walkthrough: Haig was the British commander-in-chief on the Western Front in the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Xeroradiography is an X-ray imaging technique, revealing internal structures invisible to the eye.

clue.text: Lust eats wee Scots: no protest here is found

indicators.note: something that eats another takes it inside itself

parts.note: a yen is a craving
sma is Scots for small or wee

explanation.surface: Desire devours small Scotsmen, and nobody complains.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-man agrees with everything a superior says, so from him no objection ever comes.

clue.text: The bug has one reacting nervously

definitions.note: the answer is the noun or verb, not the participle

parts.words: The bug has one reacting nervously
parts.note: surface reading: an insect or germ carries something with it; setter's reading: the dance called the bug has a first part, a word for a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: An insect that is twitchy and nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: The jitterbug is a lively swing dance; the bug in question has the answer in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A jitter is a fit of nervous shaking, the restless state of someone reacting anxiously.
